blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Physics-based soccer characters must perform diverse motor skills and transition smoothly between them, such as dribbling into a shot. However, skills that perform well in isolation may fail when executed sequentially, as preceding behaviors can leave the character and ball in unfamiliar states. We present MESSI (Multi-Expert Soccer Skill Integration), a framework that enables multiple soccer skill transitions through shared adaptation while preserving the original skill policy outside transitions. MESSI first trains eight task-competent experts using motion priors and task rewards, then distills them into a unified, skill-conditioned Transformer. Rather than retraining individual experts for different transitions, we train a shared, context-conditioned low-rank adapter on the frozen student through online reinforcement learning. Activated upon skill switching, the adapter helps the target skill handle unfamiliar entry states, while a learned exit mechanism determines when to return control to the original student. By disabling the adapter during native skill execution, MESSI preserves the original student policy by construction. Experiments across individual skills, skill transitions, and continuous skill chains demonstrate substantial improvements over direct switching, including an increase in dribbling-to-shooting success from 19.8% to 61.8%.
blocks.zh: 基于物理的足球角色必须表现出不同的运动技能并平稳地在他们之间过渡,如被打入一发. 然而,孤立状态下表现良好的技能在相继执行时可能会失败,因为之前的行为会让角色和球留在陌生状态. 我们提出MESSI(多专家足球技能一体化),这是一个框架,通过共享适应,能够实现多种足球技能过渡,同时在过渡之外保留原有的技能政策。 MESSI首先利用运动前科和任务奖励培训了8位任务能力专家,然后将其分解成统一,技能条件的变形器. 我们通过在线强化学习,在被冻结的学生身上培训一个共同的、符合具体情况的低级适配器,而不是为不同的过渡再培训个人专家。 在技能切换后激活,适配器会帮助目标技能处理不熟悉的入场状态,而学习的出场机制则决定何时将控制还给原生. MESSI通过在本土技能执行中使适配器丧失能力,通过建筑保留了原有的学生政策. 跨个人技能、技能过渡和连续技能链的实验显示,直接转换比直接切换有很大的改进,包括弹簧射入成功率从19.8%提高到61.8%。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Soccer presents a challenging setting for physics-based character control, combining whole-body coordination with precise interactions with a dynamically moving ball [ Hong et al., 2019 , Liu et al., 2022 , Haarnoja et al., 2024 , Kim et al., 2025 , Ye et al., 2026 ] . A versatile soccer character must perform diverse skills, including locomotion, dribbling, shooting, passing, and trapping, while transitioning between them at speed. For example, a player may shoot immediately after dribbling or receive a pass while running. Such transitions are challenging because the character’s posture, momentum, and ball configuration depend on the preceding behavior and may differ substantially from the states encountered during the target skill’s training. Consequently, even well-trained individual skills can fail when executed sequentially, as illustrated in Figure 2 .
blocks.zh: Soccer为基于物理学的字符控制提供了一个具有挑战性的设置,将全身协调与精确的相互作用与动态运动球结合[Hong等,2019年;Liu等,2022年;Haarnoja等,2024年;Kim等,2025年;Ye等,2026年]. 一个多才多艺的足球角色必须具备不同的技能,包括运动、打鼓、射击、传球和陷阱,同时以快快的速度相互过渡。 例如,玩家在抛出后可以立即射击,或在跑步时收到通行证. 这种转变具有挑战性,因为角色的姿势、动力和球的配置取决于前述行为,并且可能与目标技能训练时遇到的状态相去甚远。 因此,如图2所示,即使训练有素的个人技能在连续执行时也可能失败。

blocks.en:
Recent advances in physics-based character control have enabled reusable motor skills through motion tracking and large-scale motion pretraining [ Peng et al., 2018 , Peng et al., 2022 , Tessler et al., 2024 , Juravsky et al., 2024 , Shi et al., 2026 ] . However, tracking reference motions alone does not guarantee task-specific ball control or reliable transitions absent from the motion data. While independently trained, task-competent experts can optimize individual skill objectives, composing their behaviors remains challenging when the target skill encounters unfamiliar body and ball states.
Existing approaches address skill transitions in several ways. Some learn skills and transitions jointly, either through unified multi-skill policies [ Ye et al., 2026 ] or augmented interaction trajectories [ Yu et al., 2025 ] . Such approaches may require revisiting joint policy training or transition data when introducing new transitions, potentially affecting previously learned behaviors. Others employ transition-aware initialization or fine-tuning using predecessor-generated states [ Kim et al., 2025 , Avinash et al., 2026 ] , coupling transition adaptation to individual skill policies. For more challenging transitions, policy composition methods additionally introduce intermediate behaviors when necessary [ Xu et al., 2025a ] , which can increase transition-specific training and maintenance overhead. While these approaches demonstrate effective skill composition, adapting a growing repertoire of skills without repeatedly modifying individual experts or introducing separate transition modules remains challenging. This motivates a shared adaptation strategy that supports diverse skill transitions while limiting interference with established skill behaviors.
blocks.zh:
物理学特性控制的最新进展,通过运动跟踪和大规模运动预训,使运动技能得以再被使用 [Peng等,2018年;Peng等,2022年;Tessler等,2024年;Juravsky等,2024年;Shi等,2026年]. 然而,仅跟踪参考运动并不能保证特定任务球的控制或运动数据缺失的可靠过渡. 虽然独立训练,任务胜任的专家可以优化个人技能目标,但当目标技能遇到不熟悉的身体和球状态时,其行为的组合仍然具有挑战性.
现有办法以几种方式解决技能过渡问题。 一些人通过统一的多技能政策[Ye等,2026]或增强互动轨迹[Yu等,2025],共同学习技能和过渡. 这类方法可能需要在引入新的过渡时重新审视联合政策培训或过渡数据,这可能会影响以往学到的行为。 其他采用过渡意识初始化或微调,采用前所生成状态[Kim等,2025年;Avinash等,2026年],结合过渡适应个人技能政策. 对于更具挑战性的过渡,政策组成方法在必要时还引入了中间行为[徐等,2025a],这可以增加针对过渡的培训和维护间接费用. 虽然这些办法显示出有效的技能构成,但是,在不反复修改个别专家或采用单独的过渡单元的情况下,调整技能的不断增长的系列仍然是有挑战性的。 这激励了一个共同的适应战略,支持不同的技能过渡,同时限制对既定技能行为的干扰.

blocks.en:
To this end, we present MESSI ( M ulti- E xpert S occer S kill I ntegration), a framework for integrating task-competent soccer skills and enabling their transitions within a unified physics-based controller. MESSI incorporates eight skills: off-ball movement, dribbling, shooting, passing, heading, trapping, stop-and-turn, and getting up. We first train skill-specific experts using motion priors, task rewards, and tailored curricula. Their behaviors are then distilled into a shared skill-conditioned student through a unified observation space.
Consolidating the experts into a single skill-conditioned policy provides a common backbone for transition adaptation. This enables different skill pairs to share a single adaptation module, rather than requiring separate adaptations of individual expert policies.
blocks.zh:
为此,我们提出MESSI(Multi-E xpert S occer S kill I ntegeration),这是整合任务胜任的足球技能,使其能在一个统一的以物理为基础的控制器内过渡的框架. MESSI包括了8个技能:离球运动,抛射,射击,通过,取向,陷阱,停转和起起起. 我们首先利用运动前科、任务奖励和量身定制的课程,培训技能专家。 然后通过统一的观测空间,将他们的行为分馏成一个具有共同技能条件的学生.
将专家合并为单一的技能政策,是过渡适应的共同支柱。 这使得不同的技能组合能够共享一个单一的适应模块,而不是要求单独调整专家政策。

blocks.en:
Our key insight is that transition adaptation is needed only after a skill switch, where the target skill encounters unfamiliar states generated by its predecessor.
Rather than modifying the target skill everywhere, we introduce a shared, gated, context-conditioned low-rank adapter on the frozen student. The gate opens when the
skill switches, and a learned exit decides when to close it, allowing the frozen student to resume control. Outside transitions, the adapter
never acts. We train the adapter through online reinforcement learning on predecessor-generated states and target-skill rewards. Conditioning the adapter on the skill pair and target command allows a single adaptation module to serve multiple transitions. New transition pairs can be incorporated into the shared adaptation process without modifying the original experts or the student backbone, avoiding the need to maintain separate transition-specific modules. This design improves transition robustness while leaving the native skills exactly unchanged.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • We develop a physics-based soccer control framework that consolidates eight independently trained, task-competent experts into a unified skill-conditioned policy, providing a shared backbone for transition adaptation. • We propose an online, shared transition adaptation method using a context-conditioned low-rank adapter, enabling joint adaptation across multiple skill pairs without retraining individual experts. • We introduce a learned exit mechanism that dynamically determines the duration of transition adaptation, allowing the controller to return to the frozen student when adaptation is no longer needed, while preserving the original policy during native skill execution.

Prior work addresses skill composition through several

Other methods adapt target skills to states generated by

While effective, extending these approaches to more

adaptation procedures.
We instead study transition adaptation after independently

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: As shown in Figure 3 , MESSI consists of three stages: skill-specific expert learning, multi-skill distillation, and unified transition adaptation. At test time, the controller receives the current character and ball states, skill label, and task command. A user or high-level planner specifies the next skill and its command at a scheduled skill switch, without requiring reference motions.
blocks.zh: 如图3所显示的,MESI由三个阶段组成:技能特异性专家学习,多技能分馏,以及统一的过渡适应. 在测试时间,控制器接收当前字符和球状态,技能标签,以及任务命令. 用户或高级计划员在预定的技能开关上指定了下一个技能及其指挥,而不需要参考动议.

blocks.en: 3.3 Unified Transition Adaptation
blocks.zh: 3.3 统一过渡适应

blocks.en: Although the distilled student preserves individual skill capabilities, directly switching skills can expose the target policy to unfamiliar body and ball states. Fine-tuning on these states may improve transitions but alter the target skill’s performance under native initialization. Our approach instead adapts the frozen student through a single shared module, with two key design choices: conditioning adaptation on the skill transition and learning when to deactivate it.
blocks.zh: 虽然被蒸馏出的学生保留了个人的技能能力,但直接切换技能可以使目标政策暴露在不熟悉的身体和球状态下. 对这些州的调整可能改善过渡,但改变目标技能在本土初始化下的表现。 相反,我们的方法是通过一个共享单元来适应被冻结的学生,其中有两个关键的设计选择:在技能过渡上设定适应条件并学习何时关闭。

blocks.en: As illustrated in Figure 3 (iii), the student executes the predecessor skill with the adapter disabled ( z t = 0 z_{t}=0 ). At a skill switch, the target skill becomes active and the adapter is enabled ( z t = 1 z_{t}=1 ) to handle the unfamiliar entry state. A learned exit policy subsequently determines when to deactivate the adapter, returning control to the original student. Native skill execution always bypasses the adapter.

blocks.en: 4.1 Implementation Details
blocks.zh: 4.1 详细执行情况

blocks.en:
All skills are simulated in Isaac Lab [ Mittal et al., 2023 ] with GPU PhysX at
240 Hz, and all policies run at 60 Hz, the frame rate of the reference motions.
The character is a 28-DoF humanoid driven by PD controllers, with shoe-shaped collision meshes for the feet. The rigid-body solver models neither aerodynamics nor rolling resistance, so we add drag and Magnus forces to the ball in flight and a constant rolling resistance on the ground. Each expert is trained on 4 NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPUs for 13 to 53 hours.
Distilling the eight experts into the 5.3M-parameter student takes about 4.4 hours on one GPU (behavior cloning followed by four DAgger rounds), and training the shared adapter takes 11.2 hours on four GPUs.
Appendix gives the physical parameters, motion
data, network architectures, and training hyperparameters.

blocks.en: 4.2 Baselines
blocks.zh: 4.2 基线

blocks.en: We compare our skill-specific experts and distilled student against TokenHSI* [ Pan et al., 2025 ] and SkillX* [ Ye et al., 2026 ] , two adapted baselines trained jointly from scratch across all eight skills using a unified Transformer policy. Both baselines follow their official network architectures and PPO configurations, using our observations, task rewards, and motion data. However, they exclude our skill-specific training strategies, including curricula, failure-weighted sampling, multi-objective advantages, and discriminator labels. To isolate the contribution of DAgger, we additionally evaluate the student trained with behavioral cloning alone.

blocks.en:
Direct switching activates the target skill without the adapter. Expert + STI fine-tunes the target expert with PPO from
predecessor-generated states, following the skill transition-based initialization

probability 0.7 and from a native initial state otherwise, and the fine-tuning uses
the same sample budget per transition as our adapter. One fine-tuned dribbling
expert serves all four transitions into dribbling. This is our reimplementation of
the published method, not PhysicsFC’s code. To study the exit, we also run our adapter checkpoint with the exit head disabled (Pers.) and with post-hoc cutoffs that close the gate a fixed time after the handover. To evaluate the role of parameter sharing, we additionally compare against a per-transition adapter baseline (Per-trans.), which trains a separate adapter for each skill pair on the same frozen student. We also include full fine-tuning (Full FT), which directly updates the unified student for transition adaptation.

Table 5 shows that strong isolated transitions do not necessarily translate into reliable skill chains. Per-transition adapters achieve only 35.0% and 35.2% completion on the two dribble–stop–dribble–kick

Figure 6 localizes failures by stage. Per-transition adaptation succeeds in only 49.4% of stop stages, followed by 74.2% success in subsequent dribbling. Replacing only its dribble-to-stop adapter with ours raises these rates to 98.8% and 98.4%, nearly recovering MESSI’s performance. This identifies one transition as a major bottleneck in the chain. For reception chains, MESSI’s failures concentrate in trapping (77.0%) and subsequent dribbling (68.0%), while later shooting and off-ball stages exceed 97%.
Full fine-tuning also struggles with off-ball continuation after shooting (67.4% vs. our 99.5% on the get-up chain). These findings reveal how failures at individual stages limit long-horizon skill composition.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented MESSI, a unified physics-based soccer controller
that integrates eight task-competent skills and adapts their
transitions through a shared, gated adapter.
Our method improves transition robustness while preserving
the original student policy during native execution.
Experiments further show that reliable skill composition
depends on overcoming specific transition bottlenecks,
rather than optimizing individual transitions in isolation.

我们介绍了MESSI, 一个统一的物理足球控制器
融合8个任务能力技能并调整其

我们的方法提高了过渡的稳健性 同时保持
原学生政策在本土处决期间。
实验进一步表明,可靠的技能构成
取决于克服具体的过渡瓶颈,
而不是孤立地优化个人过渡。

blocks.en:
The student observes the union of the expert observations (Table 8 ).
All quantities are expressed in the heading frame of the character, and the

token. The tokens are then processed by a Transformer encoder, whose attention is
masked so that every token other than proprioception attends only to itself and to
the proprioception token. The output tokens are concatenated and mapped to the 28-D
action mean by an MLP with one hidden layer of 1024 units.

with the action of the corresponding expert. The data are aggregated across rounds.
After each round, the student is reinitialized and trained from scratch on all
collected data, with a refitted observation normalizer and 5% of the samples held out
for validation. The loss is the mean squared error between the normalized action means
of the student and the expert.

Each skill is evaluated on 1,024 fixed cases drawn from the initial states and

facing. Both are averaged over all frames of the episode, including the transients
after each command change. The failure rate counts episodes that end in a failure.
For the kicks, the launch velocity is the ball velocity at the detected strike
(Appendices C.3 – C.5 ), and the azimuth error is
the planar angle between the launch and the commanded velocity.

blocks.en:
When two methods are evaluated on the same cases, we compare them with a two-sided
exact sign test. Cases in which both methods succeed or both fail are discarded. If
the methods were equally good, each remaining case would favor either method with
probability 1/2, and we call a difference significant if p < 0.05 p<0.05 under this
assumption. The test accounts only for the variation over evaluation cases. Every
trained policy comes from a single training seed, so the test does not cover the
variation between training runs.

Most episodes start from one of 30 receiving clips, between 0.2 and 1.2 s before the
clip’s first ball contact, but not before the start of the clip. The clips are sampled
with difficulty-weighted probabilities as for off-ball movement, and the six chest
clips carry 54% of the base weight. A serve replaces the ball of the clip and keeps
its class. The ball reaches a random point 0.2–1.0 m ahead of and up to 0.5 m beside
the character of the clip (chest balls: 0.1–0.35 m and 0.2 m), coming from within ± 90 ∘ \pm 90^{\circ} ( ± 45 ∘ \pm 45^{\circ} ) of the character’s facing. It arrives at the contact time
of the clip, or up to 0.5 s later for balls that come from 60 ∘ 60^{\circ} to 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} off
the initial facing. Ground balls roll at 4–12 m/s. Aerial foot balls arrive at
4–12 m/s and descend at 10 10 – 60 ∘ 60^{\circ} , and chest balls arrive at 7–12 m/s and
descend at 10 10 – 45 ∘ 45^{\circ} . Their arrival height is the contact height of the clip ± 0.25 \pm 0.25 m, clamped to 0.3–0.85 m for aerial foot balls and to 1.0–1.35 m for
chest balls. The launch state is found by integrating the ball model, with drag and
rolling resistance, backward from the meeting point. In 30% of episodes, the
character instead starts from one of 14 standing clips, and a foot or chest ball, with
equal probability, arrives 0.5–1.2 s later from within ± 90 ∘ \pm 90^{\circ} . It reaches a
point up to 1.5 m ahead and 1.0 m to the side (chest balls: 0.8 m and 0.3 m).
Serves are biased toward hard cases. About a third take their bearing from the outer 10 ∘ 10^{\circ} of the range, 20% of the training resets replay a recent failure, and
another 30% use narrower ranges. These ranges are the top level of two success-gated
serve curricula, at which the final expert is fine-tuned.

Figures 9 and 10 provide additional qualitative comparisons of

We evaluate continuous steering and ball control on a slalom course with varying pole spacing.
At 4.0 m spacing, our student achieves 48% success, compared with 33% for SkillX* and 0% for TokenHSI*. However, SkillX* performs better on tighter courses with 3.0 m and 2.5 m spacing (47%/30% versus our 5%/0%). Our failures are consistent with the heading bias and delayed steering response inherited from the dribbling expert, highlighting a limitation of the underlying skill rather than transition adaptation.

Table 18 repeats Table 5 with a strict test for the kick. The kick must also use the commanded foot when
shooting, launch within 10 ∘ 10^{\circ} of the commanded azimuth, and reach at least half
the commanded speed. Chain success is then bounded by kick accuracy, and every method
completes far fewer chains. Our controller is no longer the best under this criterion.
Full FT leads on the two stop-and-turn chains (85.0% and 28.7%, against our 64.8%
and 18.8%), and Per-trans. leads on the chains that start with trapping or get-up
(26.8%, 15.6%, and 55.3%, against our 19.1%, 11.3%, and 35.2%). Both kick more
accurately after dribbling than our shared adapter. Neither leads under the main
criterion, however: Full FT completes far fewer of the chains with trapping or get-up,
and Per-trans. far fewer of the stop-and-turn chains (Table 5 ).
SkillX completes many chains under the main criterion but almost none under the
strict one, so its kicks rarely meet the command. The strict rates of our controller
match those of the persistent adapter, so the exit does not cost kick accuracy.

blocks.en: Appendix E Limitations and Future Work
blocks.zh: 附录E 限制和今后的工作

blocks.en:
MESSI adapts only the 11 trained transitions,
and unseen skill switches may fail.
Several trained transitions remain challenging,
particularly trap-to-dribble and dribble-to-pass.
The student also inherits limitations of its experts,
including weak heading and delayed dribbling
responses.
blocks.zh:
MESI只适应11个训练有素的过渡,
和看不见的技巧开关可能失败。
一些经过培训的过渡仍然具有挑战性,
特别是陷阱到地上 和地上下地上。
学生还继承其专家的限制,
包括低头和延迟抛射
回应。

blocks.en:
Our chain-completion metric emphasizes continuous
execution rather than precise kicking commands,
and stop-and-turn is evaluated by ball stopping
rather than the full turning maneuver.
Furthermore, the learned exit rarely deactivates
the adapter during dribbling and kicking.

而不是完全转弯
此外,学到的退出很少停止
适配器在摇摆和踢踢时。

blocks.en:
Training requires skill-specific rewards, curricula,
and manually defined handover conditions.
Adding a new skill requires expert training,
student redistillation, and adapter retraining.
All experiments are conducted in simulation.

培训需要特定技能的奖励、课程、
和人工定义的移交条件。
增加新的技能需要专家培训,
学生重新定居 适应者再培训
所有实验都是在模拟中进行的.

blocks.en:
Future directions include learning high-level skill
selection, extending adaptation to unseen transitions,
improving rare behaviors, and supporting multiplayer
control and physical humanoids.
blocks.zh:
未来方向包括学习高水平技能
选择,将适应扩展为无形的过渡,
改善罕见的行为,并支持多人游戏
控制与物理人类。
